# `aitbc http call`

Call an AITBC HTTP endpoint by service name and path.

## Usage

```bash
aitbc http call [OPTIONS] SERVICE PATH
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `service` | text | yes | — |
| `path` | text | yes | — |

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--method`, `-X` | text | `GET` | no | HTTP method (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) |
| `--params` | text | — | no | JSON object of query parameters |
| `--body` | text | — | no | JSON object request body |
| `--url` | text | — | no | Override the service base URL |
| `--api-key` | text | — | no | API key header (X-API-Key; X-Trading-Api-Key with --auth trading) |
| `--auth` | choice | `none` | no | Use configured API key for auth ('miner' = coordinator/miner key, 'rpc' = blockchain RPC key, 'trading' = trading service key) |
| `--timeout` | integer | `30` | no | Request timeout in seconds |
| `--idempotency-key` | text | — | no | Idempotency-Key header for write requests; enables safe retry of ambiguous outcomes |
| `--expect-status` | integer (multiple) | — | no | HTTP status codes to treat as an expected answer (repeatable); prints {'status', 'detail'} and exits 0 |
| `--output` | choice | — | no | Output format (alias for --format) |
| `--format` | choice | — | no | Output format |

## Examples

```bash
aitbc http call SERVICE PATH
aitbc http call SERVICE PATH --output json
```
